input.quote: Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I ("Developed Software").
input.rationale: Section 10.4 vests ownership of all custom work of authorship in M&I expressly "even if paid for by Customer", and Customer's only right in M&I software and modifications under 17.2 is use "during the Term to process its data", so we hold no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to the Developed Software we fund. That fails the fallback on a material term. Rewriting ownership to the preferred position cannot pass the minimality gate, so we land at the fallback: one concise sentence confirming M&I owns its generic tools and know-how and granting Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for its business. Customer Data ownership in 17.1 is favourable and untouched, and 10.4's refund/credit mechanic is preserved.

ops.text: M&I owns its generic tools and know-how, and hereby grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Rather than reopen ownership, we have added one sentence giving us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for our business, while confirming M&I keeps its generic tools and know-how. This is our fallback IP position and leaves 10.4's refund/credit mechanic intact.
proposal.summary: M&I keeps generic tools and know-how; Customer gets a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Developed Software
